5. Mahajanpadas

Subject: MOC - history (Ancient)

Content

  • Aryans are considered the most powerful tribes during the Vedic period, and gradually transitioned to "Mahajanapadas" (great kingdoms) by the end of later Vedic Period. By forming territorial units called "Janapadas".

Aryans → Tribes → Jana → Janapadas → Mahajanapadas (consolidation of Jana (Aryans))

MAHAJANAPADAS

  • Total: 16 Mahajanapadas

Sources

  • Texts: Ashtadhyayi (in Sanskrit) written by Panini (oldest book on Sanskrit Grammar written in 4th-6th Century BC).

Buddhist Literature

  • Anguttara Nikaya (A total of 16 Mahajanapadas are mentioned in it).
  • Digha Nikaya (A total of 12 Mahajanapadas are mentioned in it).

Jain Literature

  • Bhagavati Sutra.
  • Mahajanapadas were either Monarchial (single decision makers) or Republic (multiple decision makers), also known as oligarchy.
  • The following Mahajanapadas were Republic → Kuru, Kamboja, Vajji, Malla, Assaka.

Map 1: Mahajanapadas Territory

  • Vajji consisted of eight clans and three of them were the most powerful kingdoms → Jnatrika, Vidha, Lichchavi.

Reasons for the Rise of Magadha

  • Its advantageous position → situated south of Ganga.
  • The capital Rajgriha was surrounded by five hills and Pataliputra was situated at the confluence of Ganga and Son.
  • The availability of large number of elephants (as it was marshy-doab region).
  • It had many great leaders.
  • Availability of Iron mines (in Jharkhand region).

DYNASTIES THAT RULED MAGADHA

HARYANKA DYNASTY

Bimbisara (544 BC-492 BC)

  • Title: Seniya
  • He led military campaign against Anga.
  • He had three wives:
  • Kosala Devi → Sister of Prasenjit (son of Kosala King)
  • Chellana (Lichchavi princess)
  • Khema → Madra Clan (Punjab)
  • He sent his physician 'Jivaka' to Ujjain (to treat King Pradyota, who was suffering from jaundice)

Ajatshatru

  • He was the son of Chellana and Bimbisara.
  • He conquered Lichchavi and Vaishali.
  • He defeated Kosala King and married his daughter.
  • He patronised the 1st Buddhist Council.
  • He later killed his father Bimbisara.
  • He was contemporary of Buddha and Mahavira.

Udayin

  • He shifted his capital from Rajgriha to Pataliputra (now: "Patna").

SHISHUNAGA DYNASTY

  • Founder: Shishunaga
  • He defeated Avanti and merged it with Magadha.
  • Kalashoka patronised 2nd Buddhist Council.

NANDA DYNASTY

Mahapadmananda

  • He was the founder of Nanda dynasty.
  • Title taken: Ekrat (Meaning: Empire builder / Uprooter of Kshatriya).

Dhananada

  • Alexander invaded India during his reign (326 BC).
  • He was the last king of Nanda Dynasty.

Battle of Hydaspes was fought between Alexander and Porus (Porus was defeated in the battle) on the banks of Jhelum (326 BC).

Society

Pottery

  • Northern black polished wares (NBPW) were used for pottery.

Coins

  • Punch-marked coins made of silver were used as the form of money for trade purposes.
  • Gold coins such as Nishka and Satmana were also used.

Trade

  • Artisans and merchants formed associations called Shrenis (Guilds) that were collectively referred to as Nigama.

Craft and Architecture

  • Craft was hereditary.
  • Iron ploughshare played a crucial role in the empire's agricultural success (second urbanization after Harappa).

Post

  • Village headman was known as Bhojaka.
  • Peasants had to pay tax called Bhaga (1/6th of their produce).
  • Gahapatis were wealthy property owners who employed slaves or hired labourers to work on their lands.
  • Bali was a voluntary offering to the King; however it was not compulsory.
  • Toll tax persisted and were collected by officers known as Shulkadhyaksha (Superintendent of tolls and customs) (corrected: Shaulkiak → Shulkadhyaksha).
